transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's my right knee, mainly. It's been aching on and off for about three years, but it's got noticeably worse over the last two months.
Could you tell me how the knee aching is affecting your everyday life, if at all, and whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
Well, I can't walk the dog round the park anymore, and going downstairs I have to take it one step at a time holding the rail. As for medicines, penicillin gives me a rash.
Could you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have started or changed recently—including the dose if you know it—and any past health problems, operations, or hospital stays?

I take metformin 1 g twice a day, aspirin 75 mg once a day, atorvastatin 40 mg at night, and ramipril 5 mg once a day. Health-wise, I've had type 2 diabetes for about ten years, and I had a stent put in a heart artery six years ago.
On a scale of 0 to 10, where 0 is no aching and 10 is the worst you can imagine, how bad is the knee aching at its worst?
On a bad day it's about a 7 out of 10.
Can you tell me anything else you’ve noticed along with the knee aching, either in your knee or anywhere else in your body?
The knee sometimes swells a little by the evening. There's no redness or fever, and it doesn't lock up.
Besides those, is there anything else you take for your diabetes or your heart, or is that all the medicine you take?
No, that's the lot. Those four are all I take.
Is there anything you’ve noticed that makes the knee aching better or worse?
It's worse going down stairs and after walking more than about ten minutes; it eases with rest and paracetamol.

Apart from the diabetes and the heart stent, is there anything else you see a doctor or nurse about regularly—including anything your medicines are for—or any past operations or hospital stays? It’s fine if there’s nothing else.
No, there's nothing else. It's just the diabetes and the heart stent I see them about, and I've not had any other operations or hospital stays.

Just to be thorough about medicines: besides the four you listed and any paracetamol you take, do you use anything at different times of day, anything that isn’t a tablet—like an inhaler, eye drops, cream, injection or patch—or anything you buy without a prescription, such as painkillers, vitamins or herbal remedies? It’s fine to say no.
No, nothing else. Just the paracetamol now and then for the knee, and I don't use inhalers, drops, creams or anything like that.
What worries you most about your knee at the moment, and what are you hoping we can help with today?
I'd like something stronger for the pain, because the paracetamol isn't really enough now. And I want to know whether I might end up needing a knee replacement.
I want to make sure I’ve got this right: you mentioned that resting and paracetamol ease your knee, but also that paracetamol no longer gives you enough relief—which is closer to how it is for you?
It does help a bit, so I don't want to say it does nothing — but it's not enough anymore. On the bad days it barely takes the edge off, which is why I'd like something stronger.
Since the knee trouble started, have you noticed any changes in your appetite, sleep, weight or energy? It’s fine to say no.
No, I can't say I've noticed anything like that. My appetite, sleep and energy all seem about the same, and my weight hasn't changed.
Since the knee trouble started, have you noticed any changes in your bladder or bowel habits, or in your breathing?
No, nothing's changed there — my bladder and bowels are as they always were, and my breathing's fine.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
